cap.n0: A million-token prompt:|about eight terabytes of memory, just to remember it.
cap.n1: That is with the textbook kind of attention,|on Llama 3's biggest size, 405 billion parameters:|about ten times the model's own weights.|So where does that memory go,|and how do real models put it on a diet?|From Prof. Yufei Ding's CSE 291P, lecture 3.
cap.n2: Quick callback to the last episode.|Every token at the attention party carries three things:|a question card, its query; a name tag,|its key; and a parcel, its value.
cap.n3: To pick the next word,|the newest token holds up its question,|checks it against every name tag,|and takes a share of every parcel.
cap.n4: And a model writes one token at a time.|Done the naive way, every time a new token arrives,|every earlier token cuts its name tag|and wraps its parcel all over again.
cap.c1: So we have to do it again and again.
cap.n5: But an old token's tag and parcel never change.|Same words, same layer, same numbers.|Making them again is pure waste.
cap.n6: Her slide says the fix in one line:|keep the old keys and values,|and only compute attention for the new token.
cap.c2: so that you do not need to do the computation again,|because they have computed already.
cap.n7: That is the KV cache. K for keys, V for values.|Picture a cloakroom: every guest who came before left|a name tag and a parcel on the wall.
cap.n8: The newcomer brings only a question card,|reads the wall, and leaves its own tag and parcel|for whoever comes next.
cap.n9: Why is there no Q cache?|Old questions are never asked again.|Only the newest token asks.
cap.n10: The catch: the wall only grows.|One more tag and parcel per token,|and for every new token,|the whole wall is hauled out of memory and read again.
cap.n11: Noam Shazeer wrote in 2019 that this hauling,|more than the arithmetic, is what makes generating slow.
cap.n12: So how big does the wall get?|Her slide gives the size for one token, as a product.|It starts with a two.
cap.c4: we want to have one copy for key and one copy for value.|So that's why we have the first two.
cap.n13: Then the number of layers.|A model is a stack of layers,|each running attention again,|so every layer, every floor of the building,|keeps its own cloakroom.|Then the KV heads. Remember heads from last time:|attention runs several copies side by side, and in plain|attention each head keeps its own|rack of tags and parcels.|Then the head size: how many numbers sit on each tag.|And 2 bytes per number, at 16-bit precision.
cap.n14: Try Llama 3's 8-billion model,|as if it used plain multi-head attention:|2, times 32 layers, times 32 heads,|times 128, times 2 bytes.
cap.n15: That is 524,288 bytes.|About half a megabyte, for every single token.|A 4,096-token prompt: about 2 gigabytes.
cap.c6: And the result we want to show here is just thinking|like you are serving just one user at one time.
cap.n16: Now the 405-billion model:|126 layers and 128 heads.|About 8.3 megabytes per token.|A million tokens: about 8.3 terabytes.
cap.n17: One note on the slide:|its last column mixes units counted|in 1,024s with units counted in 1,000s.|In plain decimal units it reads 524 gigabytes,|2.6 terabytes and 8.3 terabytes.
cap.n18: That 405B model, released as Llama 3.1,|stops at 128K tokens:|the million is a thought experiment.|So is the plain attention:|Llama 3 itself does not use it.
cap.c7: They are not using it today because it's too costly.
cap.n19: So the fix starts from the formula.|Layers and head size come with the model's design.|The KV heads are the factor to change.|In plain multi-head attention,|every head gets a private rack: 32 heads, 32 racks.
cap.n20: Shazeer's idea was multi-query attention.|Every head keeps its own question,|but they all share one rack: one KV head.|The cache shrinks 32 times on the 8-billion model,|and 128 times on the 405-billion.
cap.c12: But the result shows it's not very good
cap.n21: Sharing has a price: quality can drop.
cap.n22: In 2023, Joshua Ainslie and colleagues|split the difference with grouped-query attention.|Heads form groups, and each group shares one rack.
cap.n23: In their paper, quality stayed|close to full multi-head attention,|with speed close to multi-query.
cap.n24: Llama 3 keeps 8 KV heads in every size.|32 heads over 8 racks:|4 times smaller. 64 over 8:|8 times. 128 over 8: 16 times.
cap.n25: Back to our giant and its million tokens:|from 8.3 terabytes down to about 516 gigabytes.
cap.n26: And one thing her slide stresses:|grouping is mainly an inference saving.|For the arithmetic, and for training, it changes little.
cap.c13: Not a huge saving.|But on the memory side, it's a huge saving
cap.n27: And memory is the hauling|that every new token waits for.
cap.n28: So: keep the keys and values, never the questions.|Size per token: two, times layers, times KV heads,|times head size, times bytes.|To shrink it, let heads share.
cap.n29: Next time:|instead of sharing the parcels, what if we zip them?
